people.name: Ella Atkins (co-advised with Ed Durfee)
people.current_position: Fred D. Durham Chair in Engineering and Head, Kevin T. Crofton Department of Aerospace and Ocean Engineering, Virginia Tech

bio.summary: Ella Atkins is head of the Kevin T. Crofton Department of Aerospace and Ocean Engineering at Virginia Tech and holds the Fred D. Durham Chair in Engineering. Earlier a professor of aerospace engineering at the University of Michigan, directing the Autonomous Aerospace Systems Lab, with a year as technical fellow at Collins Aerospace. Research covers AI-enabled autonomy, flight planning and control for uncrewed aircraft and advanced air mobility.
bio.thesis_title: Plan Generation and Hard Real-time Execution with Application to Safe, Autonomous Flight
notable: Editor-in-Chief, Journal of Aerospace Information Systems

people.name: Tarek Abdelzaher
people.current_position: Sohaib and Sara Abbasi Professor of Computer Science, University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign

bio.summary: Tarek Abdelzaher is the Sohaib and Sara Abbasi Professor of Computer Science at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign. Research spans real-time computing, cyber-physical systems, social sensing, IoT and edge AI. Received a Ph.D. from the University of Michigan in 1999 under Kang G. Shin and served as Editor-in-Chief of the Journal of Real-Time Systems for 20 years.
notable: IEEE TCRTS Outstanding Technical Achievement and Leadership Award (2012)

bio.summary: Sunghyun Choi is a Professor at KAIST School of Electrical Engineering, where he directs the AI-Native Networking Lab. Previously Executive Vice President and head of the Advanced Communications Research Center at Samsung Research (2019-2025), and professor of ECE at Seoul National University (2002-2019). Contributed to IEEE 802.11 WLAN standards and works on wireless networking, 6G and AI-native networks.

people.name: Xi Zhang
people.current_position: Professor and Founding Director of the Networking and Information Systems Laboratory, ECE, Texas A&M University

bio.summary: Xi Zhang is a full professor in Electrical and Computer Engineering at Texas A&M University and founding director of its Networking and Information Systems Laboratory. Holds a Ph.D. from the University of Michigan advised by Kang G. Shin, and worked earlier at AT&T Bell Labs. Research covers statistical delay-bounded QoS provisioning, 5G/6G wireless, edge computing and finite blocklength coding.
notable: Multiple IEEE GLOBECOM best paper awards
